title: Capabilities and protocol
purpose: Before a client searches, it asks the host what it is and what it serves: the three capabilities documents name the index, its k, the limits and the features a client may rely on, and the transport rules say how a request must be written and how an answer is encoded. The chapter's evidence is of I.2's first kind, a complete expected answer: the documents are compared field by field with the manifest's pinned facts of this index and with one another on their shared fields, and each transport rule is exercised once; all of it on the direct access paths, since the MCP tools expose the service's documents, not the host's.

intro: Three GET routes describe the host (SPEC-pattern-search section 23.1, SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 10.3). A client decides from them which features it may use: this *client feature-availability check* reads a field's presence and value, never a null as false, and has nothing to do with the *deploy gate* of this report, which is a release-policy decision over the run's outcomes (I.1, appendix F). The map below says what each document is for, what shape it has and which of its fields must agree with another's. The `same_answer` relations compare the named shared paths of two documents, or a projection of one onto the other, never the two whole documents, which is why documents of different shape pass them. The transport of `POST /pattern` (section 3): one RFC 8259 JSON text with unique member names and nothing after it, else 400 `invalid_request`; the answer compact JSON, gzip or deflate when `Accept-Encoding` asks; error bodies never compressed; a single-graph server answers on its graph. `/resolve` and `/traverse` share the request pool and the JSON rules.

intro: Ground truth. The expectations of C-caps are the manifest's pinned facts of this index (`index_fp` as the pinned capabilities snapshot states it, `k` 31, regime and graph mode basic, mask file, counting exact, placement record, support `record_verified`, `pattern_contract_version` 1) and the SPEC's fixed values (`routes.pattern`, `details`); the three `same_answer` relations compare the documents with one another on the paths of the map above, and on those alone. C-protocol searches one 25 bp window of eco under each transport variant; the refusals carry the host's code, and the two GET-on-POST tests accept 400, 404 or 405.

Via MCP the chapter is out of reach by construction: the tools build the HTTP request themselves (headers, body, method), so no protocol scenario can be expressed, and the capabilities tools answer the service's own documents, which carry the service's gate, backends and presets, not the host's fields. Appendix B names the four cases.

C-caps.title: capabilities
C-caps.prose: The three documents, one test each (`capabilities_doc`): `/traverse/capabilities` states its identity and limits (`release`, `index_fp`, `k`, `max_query_bp`, `max_seeds`, the attempts' `server_instance`), the gate block with `pattern_contract_version` 1, `available` true and `details` naming `GET /pattern/capabilities`, `index_fp` equal to the pinned one, `k` 31 and `regime` basic, the whole within 32 KiB; `/pattern/capabilities` carries the full block (`caps`, `mismatches`, `predicate`, `genetic_codes`, `default_max_anchors`) with the index's graph mode, mask, counting, placement, support and the default projection; `/capabilities` is ready, in single mode, with its features, routes (the pattern routes named as section 23.1 says), the pattern block, the resolve bounds, `release` and `server_instance`. The relations (`same_answer` on named paths, printed under the table) tie the three together. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every access path: {footnoted_text}. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]] [[n_relations ? Of the {n_relations:word} relations, {relations_text}.]] Via MCP the tools answer the service's own documents or nothing (see B); the host's fields the check reads are not in their answers, so no document claim is tested there[[n_mcp_not_exercised ?, and !!{n_mcp_not_exercised:word} test{n_mcp_not_exercised:s} [[n_mcp_not_exercised = 1 ? is | are]] not exercised at all!!]].
C-caps.claim: the three capabilities documents state the pinned identity, limits and gate block, agree with one another on their shared fields, and the probe document stays within 32 KiB

C-protocol.title: protocol
C-protocol.prose: The transport rules of section 3 and the refusals of section 6, one request each: `Accept-Encoding` gzip answers a gzip body (`content_encoding`) that still holds the window's contexts (`contains_source_context`), deflate a deflate body; an error body is never compressed (an unknown field under `Accept-Encoding` gzip: 400 `invalid_request` with no `Content-Encoding`); a JSON text with a comment, a duplicated member name and a body that is not an object are 400 `invalid_request`; a wrong `Content-Type` (text/plain) is still read as JSON (code-derived: the route parses the body whatever the header says); and GET on `POST /pattern` and on `POST /resolve` is not served (400, 404 or 405). The headers are read on the direct access paths only. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every access path: {footnoted_text}. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]] [[mcp_all_not_exercised ? !!Not exercised via MCP!!: the tools build the HTTP request themselves (see B). | Via MCP: {mcp_classes_text} (see B).]]
C-protocol.claim: the host negotiates gzip and deflate, never compresses an error body, refuses non-RFC 8259 JSON and non-object bodies, reads JSON under a wrong content type and does not serve GET on a POST route

C-caps.property: The three capabilities documents state the pinned identity, limits and the gate block; /traverse/capabilities stays within 32 KiB; the documents name the same server, /capabilities' pattern block is the /pattern/capabilities document and the gate block projects it (relations same_answer).
C-caps.question: Do the three capabilities documents state this index's pinned identity, limits and gate block, agree on their shared fields, and keep the probe within 32 KiB?

C-protocol.property: gzip and deflate negotiation on a /pattern answer; an error body uncompressed; a comment, a duplicated member name and a non-object body refused 400; a wrong content type still read as JSON; GET on a POST route not served (400, 404 or 405).
C-protocol.question: Does the host negotiate gzip and deflate, leave an error body uncompressed, refuse malformed JSON and non-object bodies, read JSON under a wrong content type, and not serve GET on a POST route?
